reader.requirement: At --std 85 a record-name (an 01 under an FD, SD or CD) must be accepted both as the qualified data-name-1 (R1 IN F1) and as a data-name-2 qualifier (X OF R1), alone or within a longer chain.
reader.edition-search: grep of DataBinder.cs, NameResolution.cs, ReferenceResolver.cs, SymbolTable.cs, ConditionBinder.cs for CobolVersion|EditionContext|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior|Edition.(DialectLevel|Edition|Year|Removed): the procedure-division qualified lookup (QualifiedCandidates -> QualifierChainMatchesFrom -> QualifierWalk, ConditionQualifierChainMatches) has no edition test; only Edition.At (cursor) and Edition.Permissive (SR1's --permissive disposition). The per-edition reserved-word gate (Frontend/Parsing/ReservationGateRewriter) decides what is a user-defined word on every path; it is not specific to qualification and no gated word was used. Record-names are ordinary DataItem roots in the same ancestor walk, with no edition or level test.

reader.notes: A record-name is the root DataItem of the ancestor chain QualifierWalk reads, so it serves as a qualifier and, as the referenced name, takes the file/cd-name as its only outer qualifier. Probed for FD, SD and CD records.

refuter.evidence: r11rec at 85 covers an FD with two records, RA and RB, each holding an X (implicit redefinition). RA OF F1 was a receiver, X OF RA OF F1 printed AB, X IN RB printed CD, RB IN F1 printed ABCD, and after MOVE 'QQ' TO X OF RB the program printed 'ABQQ QQ', which is the shared area. r12recneg: 'X OF F1' was refused (2 declarations of 'X' match), as were 'RA OF RA' and 'X OF RB OF RA' (a sibling record as qualifier). The reader's q85cd covers the SD and CD records. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.5 ... the text is in SRL2.5'.
